cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, which is the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here is about sweep TIMING and not about the defect. That must be read in-guest before it is called either way.

title: a reorder array held interior pointers into a picture buffer that was freed wholesale
object: the H264 DPB, ONE av_mallocz_array block, with delayed_pic[] holding &DPB[i]
lifetime_ender: av_freep(&h->DPB), which frees the whole block in one call
shape: an array of interior pointers into a single block freed as a whole
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, with no pool or refstruct layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is `h->delayed_pic[i]->reference = 0;`, a WRITE through an interior pointer.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: the function moved to n9.0.1:libavcodec/h264dec.c, which clears the reorder array with `memset(h->delayed_pic, 0, sizeof(h->delayed_pic));` before freeing the DPB. That memset is absent at e8714f6f93d1^.
nested_why: the object came straight from av_malloc/av_mallocz/av_malloc_array/av_realloc -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool, AVRefStructPool or other recycling layer between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../pool-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the dangling pointers are INTERIOR -- `&h->DPB[i]` for various i -- into one allocation freed in a single call, so clearing the owning pointer cannot help and the fix must clear the other ARRAY. It is also a WRITE, which makes it the most damaging shape here: it stores into whatever now occupies the block rather than merely reading it.
